title: Reclaiming the Record: AI, Community Datasets, and Cultural Memory
body:
### Reclaiming the Record: AI, Community Datasets, and Cultural Memory

###### Join us for a virtual panel exploring how ancestral, DIY, and community archival practices are reshaping digital memory work.

###### **How is this going to go?**

We will be joined by [Gustavo Nogueira de Menezes](https://us.list-manage.com/u0YVUPs-N_y?e=e1eaf5131a&c2id=5f077dbf08939a044ca1124728684940) (AI X Design/ Temporality Lab), [Ayoola Gbade-Bello](https://us.list-manage.com/PEWIuxTOqMa?e=e1eaf5131a&c2id=5f077dbf08939a044ca1124728684940) (Kintrace AI), and [Ethel-Ruth Tawe](https://us.list-manage.com/2OO1uM9IoaZ?e=e1eaf5131a&c2id=5f077dbf08939a044ca1124728684940)(Contemporary& / Listening to Images) for a roundtable discussion on AI x Memory. Each guest will share a provocation from their work and this will be followed by an open discussion with attendees.



**Bios:**




**Gustavo Nogueira de Menezes**

Gustavo Nogueira de Menezes (he/they) is a Temporality Researcher from the Amazon Rainforest and founder of Temporality Lab. Specialising in temporalities and decolonial perspectives, Gustavo helps individuals and societies reflect on change using ancestral and contemporary methods.

Based in Amsterdam, he collaborates with companies like Globo, Google, Natura, Netflix, Nubank, and Spotify. His research with IAM Internet & AIxDesign explores AI’s impact on time perception and Ancestral AI. His work addresses social change, ancestry, speculative design, and decoloniality, offering insights into time’s influence on human experience and encouraging a rethinking of our relationship with time.




**Ethel-Ruth Tawe**

Ethel-Ruth Tawe (b. Yaoundé, Cameroon) is an antidisciplinary artist and creative researcher exploring memory in Africa and its diaspora. Image-making, storytelling, and time-travelling compose the framework of her inquiry. From photography, collage, and text, to moving image, installation and other time-based media, Tawe examines culture and technology often from a speculative lens. Her burgeoning curatorial practice took form in an inaugural exhibition titled 'African Ancient Futures', and continues to expand in a myriad of audiovisual experiments. She is currently Editor-in-Chief at Contemporary And (C&) Magazine.




**Ayoola Gbade - Bello**

Ayoola is the founder of [@kintraceai](https://www.instagram.com/kintraceai/) Technologies, an AI-powered storytelling and heritage platform helping multicultural families preserve memories and identities across generations. His eight-year journey began in 2017 while curating a family’s 138-year history, a moment that sparked his passion for legacy preservation. From recording his own father’s story to navigating marriage, fatherhood, and a move from Nigeria to Canada, Ayoola has lived the importance of safeguarding family stories. His father’s passing in 2024 strengthened his mission: ensuring no story is ever lost. A graduate of Waterloo’s MBET program, his work sits at the intersection of AI, storytelling, and cultural heritage, with support from INSEAD AI Venture Lab, Communitech, Velocity, and Google Cloud.
